items.title: Shocking secret you won't believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines: An eye-tracking analysis

judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this paper is to fill a gap in the literature by providing empirical evidence of how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses, specifically emotional arousal and intention to read news.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que investiga os efeitos de manchetes clickbait em usuários, conforme solicitado. Os dados extraídos sobre o método e os achados estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence of the effects of clickbait on online users.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do tema solicitado (efeitos de clickbait em usuários), é um estudo empírico (experimento), o método descrito condiz com o resumo e os achados extraídos são sustentados pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Decoding Clickbait: The Impact of Clickbait Types and Structures on Cognitive and Emotional Responses in Online Interactions

judge.evidence_topic: This study delves into the influence of clickbait types (hyperbole, insinuation, visual rhetoric, and puzzle) and structures (emotion-label and emotion-laden words) on user cognitive and emotional responses in an online environment.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using electroencephalography with 32 internet-experienced participants, we analyzed how these different clickbait configurations affect engagement and processing.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que utiliza EEG para medir respostas cognitivas e emocionais de usuários a diferentes tipos de clickbait, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão e exclusão. O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Superlatives, clickbaits, appeals to authority, poor grammar, or boldface: Is editorial style related to the credibility of online health messages?

judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to understand how different ways of editing health-related messages affect their credibility among adolescents... True messages with and without editorial elements were perceived as equally trustworthy, except for news with clickbait headlines, which were less trustworthy than other true messages.
judge.evidence_empirical: The sample consisted of 300 secondary school students ( M age = 17.26; SD age = 1.04; 66.3% female). To examine the effects of manipulating editorial elements, we used seven short messages about the health-promoting effects of different fruits and vegetables.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que investiga o efeito de manchetes clickbait na percepção de credibilidade de mensagens de saúde por adolescentes, atendendo aos critérios. O tamanho da amostra e o método descritos no resumo coincidem com os dados extraídos. O achado principal é sustentado diretamente pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Did clickbait crack the code on virality?

judge.evidence_topic: we challenge the popular belief that clickbait systematically leads to enhanced sharing of online content on social media. We confirm that, on average, clickbait articles elicit far fewer shares than non-clickbait articles.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using a controlled experiment, we confirm that high-emotional headlines are shared more and show evidence that clickbait often leads to inferences of manipulative intent and source derogation. We then use a well-known secondary data set containing 19,386 articles from 27 leading online publishers.
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico, utiliza experimento e análise de dados de compartilhamento para avaliar o efeito do clickbait no comportamento do leitor, estando alinhado ao pedido. O achado principal está explicitamente presente no resumo.

items.title: Seeing is not always believing: an exploratory study of clickbait in WeChat

judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this study is to unpack the antecedents and consequences of clickbait prevalence in online media at two different levels, namely, (1) Headline-level: what characteristics of clickbait headlines attract user clicks and (2) Publisher-level: what happens to publishers who create clickbait on a prolonged basis.
judge.evidence_empirical: the authors collected longitudinal data in collaboration with a leading company that operates more than 500 WeChat official accounts in China. This study proposed a text mining framework to extract and quantify clickbait rhetorical features (i.e. hyperbole, insinuation, puzzle, and visual rhetoric). Econometric analysis was employed for empirical validation.
judge.reason: O artigo utiliza dados longitudinais de cliques e tráfego de usuários para analisar os efeitos do clickbait, o que se enquadra perfeitamente no critério de estudo empírico com dados de engajamento. O estudo não é um modelo de detecção, mas uma análise econométrica dos efeitos.

judge.evidence_topic: this research explores how credible news outlets directly engage with their respective audiences by framing push notifications in the form of clickbait.
